coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Budget; no search run.

coverage.found: Control of Slaughter-houses Act 1964: slaughterhouse licence expires each 31 Dec (annual renewal); Veterinary Public Health Act 2013 (Act 17 of 2013) covers approval/inspection of slaughter facilities. Small niche; weak candidate.

coverage.found: Budget; no search run.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction

coverage.found: EEA issues waste management licences under Waste Regulations 2000 (reg 18); EEA general-waste application form updated July 2026; 53 applications in one quarter of 2023. See candidate under 32.

coverage.found: Budget; no search run.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Budget; no search run beyond the livestock traceability item.

coverage.category: 31. Liquor and trading licences (Liquor Licences Act 1964; Trading Licences Order 1975, local authorities)
coverage.found: Liquor Licences Act 1964 has period-of-licence provisions (Liquor Licensing Board); Trading Licences Order 1975 as amended 2011; licence-renting to foreigners on Nation Land carries a E15,000 fine; Trading Licences Order (Amendment) Bill 15 of 2020 status unknown. No 2024-27 Act found.

coverage.category: 32. Environment Authority waste licensing and environmental audits (Waste Regulations 2000; Environment Management Act 2002)
coverage.found: Waste licences cover general, hazardous, clinical, reclamation/recycling; the application form requires an expenditure plan; operators must follow annual waste management plans (per a secondary summary). Form updated July 2026.

coverage.category: 33. Mandatory EFD / TaxCore e-invoicing (Legal Notice 111 of 2026 and Electronic Submission of Fiscal Data Notice, in force 15 Jul 2026)
coverage.found: Specified taxpayers must use accredited EFDs and transmit fiscal data to the ERS e-invoicing system in real time, or within 15 days after a connectivity or power failure. Phased by sector, wholesale and retail first (ERS workshop 24 Jul 2026). Third-party trackers say ERS launched the TaxCore programme on 11 May 2026 and full rollout is targeted for Jan 2028; one gives a different notice number (270 of 2026, effective 3 Jul 2026). No accredited-supplier list published yet. See K01/K02/K08.

coverage.category: 34. Dairy Board permits and licences (Dairy Act 1968; Dairy Regulations 2021)
coverage.found: Dairy Board issues permits and licences for production, import, export, marketing and distribution of dairy products. Small niche; recurring duties not seen.

coverage.category: 35. NPO Bill 2024 / NGO registration
coverage.found: Bill pending, not enacted by the 2026 sources found. Civil-society critics expect expanded state oversight. Watch item.

coverage.category: 36. Cannabis and hemp licensing
coverage.found: Hemp reportedly still illegal (June 2026 compliance site); the Cannabis Bill is unenacted. Only one legacy licensed grower (Profile Solutions, 2019 release). No buyer base.

coverage.category: 37. Foreign worker permits and employer duties (Immigration; quota system)
coverage.found: Permits are role-specific, 1-2 years, renewable, with sector quotas. Sources are commercial guides that conflict on the issuing ministry. Dominated by EOR vendors. Weak.

coverage.category: 38. Workmen's Compensation Act 1983 employer duties
coverage.found: The 1983 Act is the only version found; a 2023 replacement could not be confirmed. Self-employed persons are excluded. No recurring employer filing identified.

coverage.category: 39. Companies Act 2009, beneficial ownership and annual returns (CIPA)
coverage.found: CIPA registry portal exists; a proposed new Companies Bill is described in a Ministry fact sheet. Beneficial ownership reported to the FIU under 2011 Acts, per an unverified blog (25% threshold unverified). Deadlines not found.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Pawnbroking Act 1894 (Act 13/1894, 1998 consolidation) still on eswatinilii: licence from district Regional Administrator, E1,000 security plus two sureties; fines up to E100. A very old, tiny regime with no recurring filing found. No second-hand dealer statute found; the Trading Licences Order 1975 (as amended 2011) is the general hook (licensing officer per district; adverts within 3 working days), but its text returned 403 so categories and renewal were not confirmed. Nothing recurring that software would serve.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: One search; no Eswatini dismantler, scrap-yard or end-of-life vehicle rule found (results were South Africa, NY and others). Falls under the general trading licence at most. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No Eswatini beekeeper registration law found. Times of Eswatini (May 2022) reports ministry training and honey export to South Africa and others under AGOA, with two local processors. EU honey rules (Reg 2023/2652 establishment listing from 29 Nov 2024, residue monitoring plan, health certificate) apply to any exporter, but no Eswatini-specific exporter lists were found. Tiny, informal sector.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: The relevant law is the Factories, Machinery and Construction Works Act 1972 (Act 17/1972), not a 'Machinery and Occupational Safety Act'. Its 'machinery' definition covers boilers, pressure vessels and lifting appliances, and it has inspectors (s.7) and factory registration. Inspection frequency, certificate and owner-record provisions were not read because the Act text returned 403. No local private inspection-body regime or software found.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Water Act 2003 (No. 7/2003): a Water Apportionment Board (s.20) grants permits under Part V and keeps registers; permits are not needed for primary purposes. KOBWA is a bi-national Komati body (revised treaty signed 13 March 2026). No private small-system or drinking-water supplier regime found; EWSC remains the only urban provider. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Pesticides Management Act 2017 (Act 14/2017), read from the FAOLEX PDF. s.27 requires a commercial licence from the Registrar to import, store, sell or transport pesticides, and to act as a pest control operator or apply pesticides for profit; renewal is by prescribed form and fee. s.39 requires anyone who imports, manufactures, packs, stores, sells or labels pesticides to keep records of pesticides and quantities and show them to the Registrar or enforcement officers on request. Recurring record-keeping duty exists, but the number of dealers is small (low hundreds at most, unverified) and no periodic return was found.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: No Eswatini private employment agency licensing regime found; only the foreign work-permit route (Immigration Act, Employment Act, Ministry of Labour and Social Security). Nothing new beyond the foreign work-permit angle already noted in the first pass.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No funeral parlour licensing or burial society regime found. Only the Swazi Graves Act 1909 (chiefs' graves) and a 60-day death registration at Home Affairs (UK FCDO). Burial societies are informal and unregulated as far as the search shows. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Two searches. No Eswatini rule on driving school or childcare/ECCDE licensing found. A consultancy brief (UNICEF-funded, Ministry of Education and Training) says the ministry lacked a current register of about 1,200 pre-schools (2012 survey), which implies weak formal registration. Nothing else beyond the Dairy Regulations 2021 already noted.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Control of Cereals Act 1959 (No. 28/1959): cereal trader licence (to buy or sell maize), miller licence and restricted miller licence; fees in the schedule are tiny (E15 and E30, likely outdated). NAMBOARD (Act 1985) requires permits to import or export maize; the National Maize Corporation issued 7-day conditional import permits at E961 per tonne in 2022, disputed by the Eswatini Millers Association (Times of Eswatini, Nov 2022). NaPHIS handles phytosanitary import permits (7 working days notice). Few operators, state-controlled; no recurring small-business filing found.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Individual practitioners register with the Medical and Dental Council (Medical and Dental Practitioners Act 1970); private clinics are licensed by the Ministry of Health (UK FCDO list, 2020). No evidence found of a state scheme, medical-aid registry or practice-number system that clinics must report to. Insurer billing in Eswatini was not identified. Unverified rather than empty.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: No Eswatini contractor register or construction council found. Only the SADC services commitments (2019): foreign installation and assembly work above E60 million needs a joint venture with a Swazi contractor with foreign ownership capped at 40%, and higher registration fees for foreign contractors. The Factories, Machinery and Construction Works Act 1972 covers construction-site safety. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: NaPHIS (naphis.gov.sz) issues phytosanitary export certificates, import permits and transit permits online (applicant needs national ID or company number). EU removed Eswatini from the list for fresh beef and game meat after FMD in Shiselweni (confirmed 20 May 2025; Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1200 of 12 June 2025), which blocks meat export traceability work for now. EU honey listing and residue plan rules apply but no Eswatini honey exporter data found. Nothing built beyond K-list ideas.
